'''Bryn Jerrel Forbes''' (born July 23, 1993) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for [[CS Vâlcea 1924 Râmnicu Vâlcea|Râmnicu Vâlcea]] of the [[Liga Națională (men's basketball)|Liga Națională]]. He played college basketball for [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State]] and [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Michigan State]], and became a reliable [[three-point field goal|three-point shooter]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Graham|last=Couch|title=MSU adds sharpshooting transfer Bryn Forbes from Cleveland State|url=http://www.freep.com/article/20140613/SPORTS07/306130118/bryn-forbes-michigan-state-basketball|website=[[Detroit Free Press]]|date=June 13, 2014|access-date=March 22, 2015|url-status=bot: unknown|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151225211015/http://www.freep.com/article/20140613/SPORTS07/306130118/bryn-forbes-michigan-state-basketball|archive-date=December 25, 2015}}</ref> He plays both [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] positions.<ref>{{Cite web|first=Melissa|last=Rohlin|url=http://www.expressnews.com/sports/spurs/article/Spurs-Forbes-still-learning-new-position-11030323.php|title=Spurs' Forbes still learning new position|work=San Antonio Express News|access-date=March 27, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/spurs-bryn-forbes-seeing-time-at-point-guard/|title=Spurs' Bryn Forbes: Seeing time at point guard|work=CBS Interactive Inc.|access-date=March 21, 2016}}</ref>

== High school career ==
Forbes averaged 13.6 points as a junior, helping [[J. W. Sexton High School|Sexton]] to a 26–2 record and a state championship. He scored 29 points in the 2011 Class B semifinals against [[Detroit Country Day School|Detroit Country Day]].<ref name=msubio>{{Cite web|url=http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/bryn_forbes_921537.html|title=Bryn Forbes Bio – Michigan State Official Athletic Site|website=www.msuspartans.com|access-date=March 13, 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170725030912/http://www.msuspartans.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/bryn_forbes_921537.html|archive-date=July 25, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Forbes averaged 19.0 points, 5.0 rebounds and 3.0 assists as a senior at Sexton. Playing alongside [[Denzel Valentine]] and [[Anthony Clemmons]], they won back-to-back Class B State Championships in 2011 and 2012. He connected on 60 three-pointers as a senior and scored 19 points in the 2012 Class B title game against Stevensville Lakeshore, adding seven assists, following a 19-point effort in the semifinals against [[Detroit Country Day School|Detroit Country Day]].<ref name="msubio" /> He was named a [[Lansing State Journal]] Dream Team member and was a Class B All-State selection for the [[Detroit Free Press]] and [[The Detroit News]].

He was not heavily recruited and did not receive any of the major attention that Denzel Valentine and Anthony Clemmons received. [[ESPN]] listed him as [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State]]'s third best recruit in the 2012 recruiting class. Forbes received a two-star recruiting grade from [[ESPN.com|ESPN]] and listed him as 85 overall (out of a scale or 0–100). He was the ranked the 92nd best shooting guard in the nation, the 77th best player in the [[Midwestern United States|Midwest Region]], and the 11th best player in the state of [[Michigan]]. He signed with [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State]], his only major offer, on August 4, 2011.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/143306/bryn-forbes|title=Bryn Forbes – Basketball Recruiting – Player Profiles – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 13, 2016}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/|title=Basketball Recruiting – Recruiting Database Search – ESPN|website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 13, 2016}}</ref>

==College career==

===Cleveland State (2012–2014)===
Forbes played his freshman year at [[Cleveland State Vikings men's basketball|Cleveland State]]. He appeared in 32 games, starting 18, averaging 12.7 points, 3.5 rebounds and 1.2 assists in 28.3 minutes. Forbes led the team in scoring among players who played in more than six games. He ranked 11th in [[Horizon League]] in scoring and eighth in three-pointers per game (2.0) and in conference games, ranked seventh in scoring (14.9 ppg) and second in free-throw percentage (.908). Forbes scored in double figures in 24 contests, including four games of more than 20 points. His season-high of 24 points came against both [[Valparaiso Crusaders men's basketball|Valparaiso]] (2/9/13), connecting on 8-of-10 shots, including 4-of-4 from three-point range, and [[Milwaukee Panthers men's basketball|Milwaukee]] (2/17/13), making 9-of-12 shots, including 4-of-7 from behind the arc. His other high scoring games came against [[Loyola Greyhounds men's basketball|Loyola]] with 22 points (1/23/13) and 21 against [[Detroit Titans men's basketball|Detroit]] (1/12/13), adding a season-high eight rebounds against the [[Detroit Titans|Titans]] and matching the [[Cleveland State Vikings|CSU]] single-game record with five three-pointers. Forbes collected eight rebounds at [[UIC Flames|UIC]] (2/2/13) and dished out a season-high five assists against [[Notre Dame College|Notre Dame]] (Ohio) (12/19/12). His successful freshman year was rewarded<ref name="msubio" /> with 2012–13 Horizon League Newcomer of the Year, Horizon League All-Newcomer Team, [[Collegeinsider.com|CollegeInsider.com]] Mid-Major Freshman All-America Team, and a two-time Horizon League Newcomer of the Week (Dec 3 and Jan. 14).

Forbes looked to improve going into his sophomore year. Still at Cleveland State, he started all 32 games in which he played, averaging 15.6 points, 3.1 rebounds and 1.7 assists in 34.4 minutes. His 15.6 points per game average led Cleveland State and ranked sixth in the Horizon League while he ranked second in the league in three-point field goals made (2.5 pg), trailing only [[Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball|Oakland]]'s [[Travis Bader]], the [[NCAA Division I|NCAA]]'s all-time leading three-point shooter. Forbes led the team to a 21–12 record and 12–4 in the [[Horizon League]].<ref>{{cite news |last1=Couch |first1=Graham |title=Michigan State vs. Cleveland State tipoff: Analysis, prediction |url=https://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/sports/college/msu/mens-basketball/2017/12/29/michigan-state-basketball-cleveland-state-tipoff/108904658/ |access-date=August 20, 2018 |work=[[Lansing State Journal]] |date=December 29, 2017}}</ref> His efficiency improved heavily as he ranked fourth in the Horizon League in three-point field-goal percentage (.424), fifth in free-throw percentage (.826) and fourth in minutes played (34.4 mpg). Forbes broke records when he established a Cleveland State single-season school record with 81 made three-pointers, making at least one three-pointer in every contest. Scoring came easy as he scored in double-figures in 26 of 32 games, including 10 contests with 20 points or more. He went perfect on his first 28 free throws of the season before missing. Season highs for scoring against both [[Notre Dame College|Notre Dame]] (Ohio) with 27 points (12/18/13), matching the [[Cleveland State Vikings|CSU]] single-game mark with five made three-pointers, and [[Detroit Titans men's basketball|Detroit]] (1/31/14), adding a season-high seven rebounds against the [[Detroit Titans|Titans]]. Forbes proved his ability to play on the big stage when he tallied 22 points and five rebounds at the [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|University of Kentucky]] (11/25/13), making 11-of-11 attempts from the foul line.<ref name="msubio" /> He earned second-team [[National Association of Basketball Coaches|NABC]] All-District 12 and second-Team All-Horizon League honors.

===Michigan State (2014–2016)===
Going into his junior year, Forbes decided to transfer. He wanted to come to [[Michigan State Spartans|Michigan State]] in part to be closer to home to take care of his young son and be near a family member with a medical issue. Forbes was granted a waiver to play for the [[Michigan State Spartans men's basketball|Spartans]] in the 2014–15 season. [[NCAA Division I|NCAA]] rules typically require transfer players to sit out one year, but the [[NCAA Division I|NCAA]] waivers are granted for athletes who transfer because of family hardship. Forbes still had two seasons of eligibility remaining at Michigan State.<ref name="Waiver">{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Austin|url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2014/08/bryn_forbes_granted_ncaa_waive.html|title=Bryn Forbes granted NCAA waiver to play immediately for Michigan State basketball|website=MLive.com|date=August 20, 2014|access-date=March 13, 2016}}</ref>

Forbes looked to make an immediate impact due to the massive turnover from the previous season. Michigan State lost guards, [[Keith Appling]], [[Gary Harris]], and [[Russell Byrd]]. Three post players who displayed shooting ability also left, [[Adreian Payne]], [[Kenny Kaminski]], and Alex Gauna.<ref name="Waiver" /> Forbes appeared in 39 games, starting 24, averaging 8.5 points, 1.4 rebounds and 1.0 assists in 26.2 minutes per game. Forbes' sharp shooting continued as he ranked fourth in the [[Big Ten]] in three-point field-goal percentage overall (.427), eighth in [[Big Ten]] games (.405), and 12th in the [[Big Ten]] in three-point field goals made overall (1.8). He scored in double figures in 14 games, including a season-high 21 points at [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] (3/1/15) and led [[Michigan State University|MSU]] in scoring in three games against [[Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Michigan]] (12/17/14; 14 points), [[Rutgers University|Rutgers]] (1/29/15; 18 points) and [[Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball|Wisconsin]] (3/1/15; 21 points). Forbes made two or more three-pointers in 19 games, including five games with four or more three-pointers, highlighted by a perfect 5-of-5 effort from behind the arc at [[Wisconsin Badgers|Wisconsin]] (3/1/15). Forbes shot a perfect 7-of-7 from the field, including 4-of-4 from three-point range en route to 18 points at [[Notre Dame Fighting Irish|Notre Dame]] (12/3/14). He ranked fourth on the team with 23 steals, highlighted by three steals at [[Nebraska Cornhuskers men's basketball|Nebraska]] (1/24/15). He shot .808 (42–52) from the foul line, ranking second on the team and shot .450 (9–20) from three-point range during [[Michigan State University|MSU]]'s [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] run to the [[Final four|Final Four]]. He scored 14 points in two [[NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship|NCAA Tournament]] games against [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] (3/20/15) in the second round and [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] (3/29/15) in the [[Elite Eight]] and scored the first five points of overtime in [[Michigan State University|MSU]]'s [[Elite Eight]] overtime victory, knocking down a three-pointer on the first possession of the extra stanza. His career-best of four assists against [[Arkansas–Pine Bluff Golden Lions and Golden Lady Lions|Arkansas-Pine Bluff]] came on December 6.<ref name="msubio" />

Forbes' senior year was one of much improvement. He became one of the country's top three-point shooters, making close to 50%.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/stats/basketball-men/d1/current/individual/143|title=Three-Point Field-Goal Percentage {{!}} DI Men's Basketball Statistics - NCAA.com|website=NCAA.com|access-date=March 12, 2016}}</ref> He was the recipient of many awards and records during his senior year at Michigan State. On March 2, 2016, Forbes hit a team and [[Big Ten Conference]] record 11 three-point field goals, while leading Michigan State to a 97–66 win over [[Rutgers Scarlet Knights|Rutgers]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Joe|last=Rexrode|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/michigan-state/spartans/2016/03/02/msu-rutgers-bryn-forbes/81246836/|title=Michigan State 97, Rutgers 66: Bryn Forbes sets Big Ten record for 3s|work=Freep.com|date=March 3, 2016|access-date=March 3, 2016}}</ref> Forbes, along with Denzel Valentine, was selected to the NCAA College Basketball Three-Point Contest following his senior year.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.collegeslam.com.prod.sportngin.com/participants?_ga=1.213032918.391393238.1459473513|archive-url=https://archive.today/20160719160844/http://www.collegeslam.com.prod.sportngin.com/participants?_ga=1.213032918.391393238.1459473513|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 19, 2016|title=PARTICIPANTS|website=College Slam|access-date=April 1, 2016}}</ref> Forbes was beaten by his teammate in the first round of the competition. Forbes was named [[United States Basketball Writers Association|USBWA]] All-District V 1st Team,<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.sportswriters.net/usbwa/news/2016/alldistrict160308.html|title=USBWA > News > 2015–16 Men's All-District Teams|work=SportsWriters.net|access-date=March 12, 2016}}</ref> Media [[List of All-Big Ten Conference men's basketball teams|All-Big Ten]] second eam,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://btn.com/2016/03/07/see-official-2015-16-all-big-ten-teams-award-winners/|title=See official 2015–16 All-Big Ten teams & award winners|website=Big Ten Network|access-date=March 12, 2016}}</ref> Coaches All-Big Ten second team,<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://btn.com/2016/03/07/see-official-2015-16-all-big-ten-teams-award-winners/|title=See official 2015–16 All-Big Ten teams & award winners|website=Big Ten Network|access-date=March 12, 2016}}</ref> and [[Portsmouth Invitational Tournament|PIT]] All-Tournament Team.<ref>{{cite web|first=Kyle|last=Austin|url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2016/04/matt_costello_bryn_forbes_win.html|title=Matt Costello, Bryn Forbes win all-tournament honors at Portsmouth Invitational|work=MLive.com|date=April 17, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}}</ref>

== Professional career ==
===San Antonio Spurs (2016–2020)===
After going undrafted in the [[2016 NBA draft]], Forbes joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]] for the [[2016 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-announce-2016-utah-summer-league-roster/|title=SPURS ANNOUNCE 2016 UTAH SUMMER LEAGUE ROSTER|work=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2016|access-date=January 3, 2017}}</ref> Heading into the Summer League, Spurs' head coach [[Gregg Popovich]] told Forbes "to shoot it" after he made 77-of-100 three-pointers at one of his NBA pre-draft workouts.<ref>{{cite web|first=Graham|last=Couch|url=https://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/sports/columnists/graham-couch/2016/07/03/couch-column-bryn-forbes-spurs-nba-summer-league/86638902/|title=Couch: Spurs make Bryn Forbes a priority; now he has to make shots|work=LansingStateJournal.com|date=July 3, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}}</ref> On July 14, 2016, he signed with the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-bryn-forbes|title=SPURS SIGN BRYN FORBES|work=NBA.com|date=July 14, 2016|access-date=July 15, 2016}}</ref> Forbes secured an opening-night roster spot after impressing the Spurs during training camp and preseason.<ref>{{cite web|first=Dan|last=Kilbridge|url=https://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/sports/college/msu/mens-basketball/2016/10/22/former-msu-sharpshooter-bryn-forbes-makes-spurs-roster/92600164/|title=Former MSU sharpshooter Bryn Forbes makes Spurs roster|work=LansingStateJournal.com|date=October 22, 2016|access-date=October 23, 2016}}</ref> Forbes played sparingly for the Spurs throughout his rookie season, spending most of his time in the [[NBA Development League]] on assignment with the [[Austin Spurs]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://gleague.nba.com/all-time-nba-assignments/|title=All-Time NBA Assignments|work=NBA.com|access-date=November 3, 2017}}</ref> On April 7, 2017, with [[Tony Parker]], [[Manu Ginóbili]] and [[Kawhi Leonard]] not playing, Forbes scored a career-high 27 points to lead the Spurs to a 102–89 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]]. Forbes, who had 64 points for the season with a game high of eight coming in, went 4 of 9 from 3-point range and also had career highs in minutes (29) and assists (six).<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400900561|title=Forbes, Spurs reserves top mostly Mavericks backups 102–89|work=ESPN.com|date=April 7, 2017|access-date=April 7, 2017}}</ref>

In July 2017, Forbes earned All-[[NBA Summer League]] Second Team honors for his efforts during the [[2017 NBA Summer League]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Ward-Henninger|first=Colin|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/2017-all-nba-summer-league-teams-lakers-rookie-lonzo-ball-earns-mvp-honors/|title=2017 All-NBA Summer League teams: Lakers rookie Lonzo Ball earns MVP honors|work=cbssports.com|date=July 18, 2017|access-date=November 3, 2017}}</ref> On November 3, 2017, he scored 22 points in a 108–101 win over the [[Charlotte Hornets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974877|title=Forbes scores 22 as Spurs beat Hornets 108–101|work=ESPN.com|date=November 3, 2017|access-date=November 3, 2017}}</ref> On November 11, he made his first career start and scored 13 points in a 133–94 win over the [[Chicago Bulls]], becoming the third undrafted player under 6-foot-4 to start a game in San Antonio franchise history, joining [[Avery Johnson]] and [[Anthony Carter (basketball)|Anthony Carter]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974934|title=Pau Gasol's 21 lead short-handed Spurs by Bulls, 133–94|work=ESPN.com|date=November 11, 2017|access-date=November 11, 2017}}</ref> He made his third career start on December 16 against the [[Dallas Mavericks]], joining Avery Johnson as only the second undrafted player under 6-foot-4 in Spurs history to start 3-plus games.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975186|title=Spurs close on 13–0 run to rally past Mavericks, 98–96|work=ESPN.com|date=December 16, 2017|access-date=December 17, 2017}}</ref> On January 28, 2018, he scored a season-high 23 points in a 113–98 win over the [[Sacramento Kings]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975483|title=Forbes' season-high 23 lead Spurs past Kings, 113–98|work=ESPN.com|date=January 28, 2018|access-date=January 28, 2018}}</ref>

On July 20, 2018, Forbes re-signed with the Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-re-sign-bryn-forbes|title=SPURS RE-SIGN BRYN FORBES|work=NBA.com|date=July 20, 2018|access-date=July 20, 2018}}</ref> In the Spurs' season opener on October 17, Forbes had 11 points in his first start at point guard for the team in a 112–108 win over the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070699|title=DeRozan leads Spurs past Wolves 112–108; Butler scores 23|work=ESPN.com|date=October 17, 2018|access-date=October 17, 2018}}</ref> On October 24, he scored 15 points in a 116–96 loss to the [[Indiana Pacers]], becoming the first starting point guard for the Spurs other than Tony Parker to score in double figures in each of his first four games since [[Maurice Cheeks]] in 1989.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070739|title=Oladipo scores 21 as Pacers rout Spurs 116–96|work=ESPN.com|date=October 24, 2018|access-date=October 24, 2018}}</ref> On November 10, he scored 13 points in a 96–89 win over the [[Houston Rockets]], thus scoring double figures in nine of 11 games to begin the season. The only other Spurs player to top that in his first three seasons was [[Tim Duncan]], who had 10 in 1998.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401070861|title=Aldridge's double-double helps Spurs hold off Rockets 96–89|work=ESPN.com|date=November 10, 2018|access-date=November 11, 2018}}</ref> On December 11, he had his first career double-double with a season-high 24 points and a career-best 11 rebounds in a 111–86 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]]. It was the first double-double of his basketball career, having never had a double-double stemming back to when he started basketball in elementary school.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071084|title=Forbes' double-double fuels Spurs by Suns 111–86|work=ESPN.com|date=December 11, 2018|access-date=December 12, 2018}}</ref> On December 13, in a 125–87 win over the [[Los Angeles Clippers]], Forbes joined [[Danny Green (basketball)|Danny Green]] and [[Gary Neal]] as the only Spurs players to score 1,000 points and make 150 3-pointers in their first 150 games with the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071098|title=Spurs earn largest win of the season, beat Clippers 125–87|work=ESPN.com|date=December 13, 2018|access-date=December 13, 2018}}</ref> In March 2019, Forbes reached 250 career 3-pointers, joining Neal and [[Dāvis Bertāns]] as the only players in Spurs history to accomplish that feat in their first three seasons with the team.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071712|title=Spurs win eighth straight as Blazers lose McCollum to injury|work=ESPN.com|date=March 16, 2019|access-date=March 17, 2019}}</ref>

===Milwaukee Bucks (2020–2021)===
On November 26, 2020, the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] announced that they had signed Forbes.<ref>{{cite web|title=Bucks Sign Torrey Craig, Bryn Forbes and Bobby Portis |url=https://www.nba.com/bucks/news/bucks-sign-torrey-craig-bryn-forbes-and-bobby-portis|date=November 26, 2020|website=NBA.com|access-date=November 26, 2020}}</ref> Forbes scored a career high 30 points against the Houston Rockets on April 29, 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Milwaukee Bucks at Houston Rockets Box Score, April 29, 2021|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202104290HOU.html|access-date=2022-02-11|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref> He averaged 10.0 points per game, 1.6 rebounds, while shooting a career high from 3-point range (45%) and from the field (47%) in the regular season.<ref name="Bryn Forbes Stats">{{Cite web|title=Bryn Forbes Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/f/forbebr01.html|access-date=2022-02-11|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref> In game 4 of the first-round series against the [[Miami Heat]], Forbes scored 22 points on efficient shooting off the bench, tying his career playoff high he set in game 2 of the same series. Notably, he outscored Heat star [[Jimmy Butler]] in the contest to clinch the series sweep.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Moberg|first=McLain|title=Former Spartan Bryn Forbes Drops 22-Points in Bucks' Series Clinching Win over Heat|url=https://www.si.com/college/michiganstate/basketball/former-spartan-bryn-forbes-drops-22-points-in-bucks-series-clinching-win-over-heat|access-date=2021-08-01|website=Sports Illustrated|language=en}}</ref> Forbes became an NBA Champion when the Bucks won the [[2021 NBA Finals]] in six games against the [[Phoenix Suns]]. He played in 20 of the Bucks’ 23 playoff games and averaged 6.6 points, 1.4 rebounds, and shot 37% from 3 in 13.7 minutes per game.<ref name="Bryn Forbes Stats"/>

===Return to San Antonio (2021–2022)===
On August 25, 2021, Forbes signed with the San Antonio Spurs.<ref>{{cite web|title=SPURS SIGN BRYN FORBES|url=https://www.nba.com/spurs/spurs-sign-bryn-forbes-0|website=NBA.com|date=August 25, 2021|access-date=August 25, 2021}}</ref> He played in 40 games for the Spurs, averaging 9.1 points in 16.9 minutes per game before he was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]].<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-19|title=Nuggets acquire Bryn Forbes from Spurs in 3-team trade|url=https://www.fox46.com/sports/ap-source-nuggets-to-get-forbes-from-spurs-in-3-team-trade/|access-date=2022-02-11|website=Queen City News|language=en-US}}</ref><ref name="Bryn Forbes Stats"/>

===Denver Nuggets (2022)===
On January 19, 2022, Forbes was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in a three-team trade involving the [[Boston Celtics]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/nuggets/denver-nuggets-acquire-bryn-forbes-three-team-trade|title=DENVER NUGGETS ACQUIRE BRYN FORBES IN THREE-TEAM TRADE|work=NBA.com|date=January 19, 2022}}</ref>

===Minnesota Timberwolves (2022–2023)===
On July 11, 2022, Forbes signed with the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/timberwolves-sign-bryn-forbes|title=Timberwolves Sign Bryn Forbes|work=NBA.com|date=July 12, 2022|access-date=July 16, 2022}}</ref> He was waived by the Timberwolves on February 9, 2023.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/minnesota-timberwolves-acquire-guards-mike-conley-and-nickeil-alexander-walker-from-utah-jazz|title=Minnesota Timberwolves Acquire Guards Mike Conley and Nickeil Alexander-Walker from Utah Jazz|work=NBA.com|date=February 9, 2023|quote=In connection with the trade, the Timberwolves have waived guard Bryn Forbes.}}</ref>

===Mets de Guaynabo (2025)===
On April 23, 2025, Forbes signed with the [[Mets de Guaynabo (basketball)|Mets de Guaynabo]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] for the remainder of the 2025 season.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Former NBA players DeMarcus Cousins, Bryn Forbes and Dewan Hernandez signed with Puerto Rican team Mets de Guaynabo for the remainder of the 2025 season|url=https://www.hoopshype.com/story/sports/nba/rumors/2025/04/23/former-nba-players-demarcus-cousins-bryn-forbes-and/84560333007/|access-date=January 30, 2026|website=hoopshype.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Santeros de Aguada (2025)===
On May 20, 2025, Forbes signed with the [[Santeros de Aguada]] of the [[Baloncesto Superior Nacional]] (BSN).<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.instagram.com/p/DJ5KBQfOJ31/?igsh=NTc4MTIwNjQ2YQ==|title=instagram.com}}</ref>

=== Aris Thessaloniki (2025–2026) ===
On July 18, 2025, Forbes signed with [[Aris B.C.|Aris Thessaloniki]] of the [[Greek Basketball League]] and the [[EuroCup Basketball|EuroCup]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Aris signs former NBA champ Bryn Forbes - Eurohoops |url=https://www.eurohoops.net/en/eurocup/1849282/aris-signs-former-nba-champ-bryn-forbes/ |access-date=2025-07-19 |website=www.eurohoops.net}}</ref> On March 2, 2026, he was released from the Greek club.

===Râmnicu Vâlcea (2026–present)===
On March 2, 2026, Forbes signed with [[CS Vâlcea 1924 Râmnicu Vâlcea|Râmnicu Vâlcea]] of the [[Liga Națională (men's basketball)|Liga Națională]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bryn Forbes (ex Aris) is a newcomer at Valcea|url=https://www.eurobasket.com/Romania/news/980454/Bryn-Forbes-ex-Aris-is-a-newcomer-at-Valcea|access-date=April 17, 2026|website=eurobasket.com|language=en}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Forbes has two sons, born in 2013 and 2016.<ref>{{cite web|last=Austin|first=Kyle|url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2015/10/bryn_forbes_michigan_state.html|title=Reunited with young son, Bryn Forbes has plenty of motivation for senior year at Michigan State|work=MLive.com|date=October 27, 2015|access-date=January 28, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Griffith|first=Mike|url=https://www.mlive.com/spartans/index.ssf/2016/03/bryn_forbes_reflects_on_basket.html|title=Bryn Forbes reflects on basketball journey, 'amazing' Michigan State fans|work=MLive.com|date=March 5, 2016|access-date=April 7, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Couch|first=Graham|url=https://www.lansingstatejournal.com/story/sports/columnists/graham-couch/2016/12/24/valentine-forbes-nba-christmas-couch-column/95790178/|title=Couch: Valentine, Forbes find a new world in NBA|work=LansingStateJournal.com|date=December 24, 2016|access-date=June 20, 2017}}</ref>

On February 15, 2023, Forbes was arrested in north-central [[San Antonio]] on suspicion of assault with bodily injury. He had reportedly engaged in a verbal argument with his girlfriend Elsa Jean, whom he later struck multiple times. The San Antonio Fire Department and Emergency Medical Services arrived at the scene and provided aid to the woman. Forbes was booked at the Bexar County Jail.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Free agent Bryn Forbes arrested on family violence charge |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/35666962/nba-bryn-forbes-arrested-family-violence-charge |access-date=March 15, 2023 |website=ESPN}}</ref>
Those charges were dismissed on July 19, 2023.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Bryn Forbes charges dismissed| date=July 19, 2023  | url=https://www.kens5.com/article/sports/nba/spurs/assault-case-against-former-spurs-bryn-forbes-dismissed/273-6c75cf57-c174-4989-bcff-d20992a45a47#:~:text=SAN%20ANTONIO%20%E2%80%94%20Former%20Spurs%20player,program%20offered%20by%20Bexar%20County. | access-date=July 31, 2023 | website=kens5.com | language=en}}</ref>

On February 13, 2024, Forbes was once again arrested on charges of assault. [https://news4sanantonio.com/news/local/former-spurs-player-arrested-on-family-violence-charges][https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/39519912/former-nba-player-bryn-forbes-arrested-family-violence-charge] According to police reports, Forbes entered the apartment of “an ex-significant other” – the mother of his two children – and proceeded to hit and choke her until she was eventually able to break free and seek authorities. Forbes reportedly fled the scene soon afterwards.<ref>{{cite web |last1=Avila |first1=Alejandro |title=Ex-Spurs Guard Faces Second Domestic Violence Arrest In A Year |url=https://www.outkick.com/sports/ex-spurs-guard-faces-second-domestic-violence-arrest-in-a-year |website=OutKick |access-date=February 13, 2024}}</ref>
